thread:
alex: Heads-up — Boxline is seeing steady 429s for the past ~18m. Spike aligns with minute boundary (xx:00). Customer reports errors across multiple regions. Example error id: req_7a3b2c.

maya: Can you paste a few example request IDs and the tenant/rpm/tpm from the dashboard? Also, is this only their prod key or multi-tenant?

alex: Tenant=boxline-prod, yes only their key. From our quick dashboard: tenant_rpm=1180, tenant_tpm=70800, tenant_limit_rpm=1200, tenant_limit_tpm=72000. Logs show repeated 429 with reason "rate_cap".

ingrid: Hmm looks like they’re right at the tpm boundary. Could be a fanout/cron at :00. Ask them for a sample of their call pattern (are they batching many small requests?).

alex: Sent a replay from customer: 60 requests in 30s pinned to :00, many concurrent streams. They say it’s a cron that hits 00s.

devon-oncall: Paging eng-sre for immediate mitigation. @eng-sre please advise if we can short-term raise tenant tpm or enable edge smoothing. :warning:

support-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-314 (auto). Notifying oncall.

maya: Mitigation options while we triage: 1) request customer to stagger cron by 30–60s 2) recommend client-side randomized jitter + exponential backoff 3) temporary quota bump for 30m while they roll a fix.

ingrid: Also check if their requests are many small messages — we can suggest combining requests or using a batch call to reduce RPM.

alex: I asked them to stagger and add jitter. They pushed a tentative fix but asked for an immediate short-term quota bump while they deploy.

devon-oncall: I can apply a one-time tpm bump to 100k for 1 hour if we want to avoid customer outage. Will need approval from infra lead.

maya: Before bumping, let's confirm there's no amplification loop (retries without backoff). Can we see client-side retry headers? Any sign of retry storms?

alex: Sample request header from their SDK: 
```
x-client-retries: 3
x-client-backoff-ms: 0
```
They had 0ms backoff. Oof.

ingrid: That's likely the culprit — tight retry loop + minute boundary equals rapid refill/empty pattern. Suggest they set backoff>=200ms and randomize +-100ms.

devon-oncall: Infra lead approved temporary bump. I applied +25% tpm for 45m: new tenant_tpm=90000. Noted in the incident.

alex: Customer confirmed errors dropped to near-zero after bump and staging jitter change. They will roll a permanent cron staggering fix in 2 hours.

maya: Post-incident action items: - add a KB entry about "cron alignment and minute boundaries" - run a quick tenant telemetry query to flag tenants that hit >=95% of tpm for >5m so CS can proactively reach out - consider adding a soft-smoothing edge feature (auto-splay around minute boundaries) as a product suggestion.

ingrid: For triage notes: root cause = tenant hitting configured tpm limit due to synchronized cron + zero-backoff retry amplification. Remediation = temporary tpm bump + client jitter + cron staggering.

alex: I'll follow up with customer with the suggested SDK patch snippet and link to the KB once we create it. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

devon-oncall: Closing slack triage thread, tracking follow-ups in #INC-2026-314 and the support ticket.

maya: Quick replay command I asked the customer to run to verify post-fix behavior:
```
# run 60 requests with 300ms random jitter
for i in $(seq 1 60); do sleep $(awk -v min=0.2 -v max=0.5 'BEGIN{srand(); print min+rand()*(max-min)}'); curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
```

alex: They ran it, results looked stable. Follow-up scheduled for tomorrow to confirm long-term fix.

support-bot: Incident #INC-2026-314 status -> monitoring.
